Ensemble FABIA: robust biclusters and factors from many FABIA runs

Source: R/fabia_ensemble.R
fabia_ensemble.Rd

FABIA results depend on the random starting values: two runs on the same data can return different biclusters. The ensemble approach runs FABIA many times and keeps only the biclusters found again and again, which are robust to the starting values (and, with sample_fraction < 1, to the samples used). This is the procedure of Chapter 10 of Kasim et al. (2016), implemented in the superbiclust and biclust packages, applied to FABIA.

Usage

fabia_ensemble(
  X,
  k = 5,
  control = fabia_ensemble_control(),
  alpha = 0.01,
  cyc = 1000,
  scale_features = TRUE,
  seed = 21,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

X

Either a single numeric matrix (features x samples) or a named list of such matrices. All matrices must share the same sample names (column names).

k

Number of factors (biclusters) per FABIA run, and the maximum number of robust factors returned.

control

Settings, see fabia_ensemble_control().

alpha, cyc

FABIA sparseness parameter and number of cycles, as for "FABIA" in run_factor_pipeline().

scale_features

Logical. If TRUE (default), each feature is z-scored before fitting. Features with zero variance become 0.

seed

Integer. Random seed (default 21).

verbose

Logical. Print progress messages (default TRUE).

Value

A list with scores (samples x factors), loadings (features x factors) and meta. meta contains:

reliability

Reliability of each returned factor (share of runs).

biclusters

For each factor, the robust bicluster: its features, samples and reliability.

groups

All groups of biclusters found: size, number of runs, reliability and whether they were kept.

similarity, tree

The Jaccard similarity matrix of all biclusters and the complete-linkage tree (plot it with plot()).

runs, control

Settings used.

Details

Each robust group of biclusters also gives a factor, so the result can be used like any other factomics method: its loadings and scores are the sign-aligned averages of the loadings and scores of the FABIA factors in the group. Factors are ordered by reliability.

This is a shortcut for run_factor_pipeline(X, methods = "FABIA_ENS", ...).

References

Khamiakova T, Kaiser S, Shkedy Z (2016). Ensemble methods and robust solutions. In Kasim A et al. (eds), Applied Biclustering Methods for Big and High-Dimensional Data Using R, Chapter 10. CRC Press.

Hochreiter S et al. (2010). FABIA: factor analysis for bicluster acquisition. Bioinformatics 26(12), 1520-1527.

See also

plot_fabia_ensemble(), factor_stability()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("fabia", quietly = TRUE)) {
  sim <- simulate_multiomics(n_samples = 40, seed = 1)
  fit <- fabia_ensemble(sim$data, k = 3,
                        control = fabia_ensemble_control(runs = 10),
                        cyc = 200, verbose = FALSE)
  fit$meta$reliability
}
